newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures climbed on Tuesday as a smaller than expected rise in US inflation in March sparked a rally in major bond markets.

Traders said French bonds got a lift from non-resident buying soon after the open and then extended their gains after the US figures, trimming the yield on the benchmark 10-year OAT as low as 5.70 percent.

Traders said flows in the cash market were relatively light although the recent curve flattening trend remained intact. Some said there had been sales of the two- and five-year BTANs ahead of Thursday's auction.
Traders said the move in the Bund market had been accentuated by US funds targetting 100.80 in the hope of triggering stops and this was helping to pull French bond futures higher as well.
The June bond future settled at 129.02, up 0.76, but then climbed as high as 129.14 on GLOBEX when the Bund future eventually reached 100.80.
PIBOR contracts also had a solid day, helped by some short covering from funds early on and the dollar-driven strength of the franc against the mark.

The bond future was up at the beginning on non-resident buying and "then clearly got another lift from the CPI figures not being as savage as some had feared," Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais said. "Going long on the curve is still working in the background."
Joanne Perez, strategist at Merrill Lynch in Paris said the recent outperformance of French 10-year bonds against Germany had probably reached its limit at minus 15 basis points.
She said the recent coupon flows had probably already been reinvested and at minus 15 domestic investors would be starting to look at mark bonds for extra yield and little currency risk.

Traders also said there had been some switching out of the two- and five-year part of the curve, both because they looked expensive compared to other BTANs and also as part of moves by investors to lengthen duration.
The gap between two- and 10-year French bonds narrowed four basis points. The 10-year spread between French and German yields was steady at minus 13 after touching minus 15 during the day.
The Treasury said on Tuesday it would be selling 22 to 24 billion francs of the two- and five-year benchmark BTANs at its regular monthly auction on Thursday.
The franc slide to its lowest level this year against the dollar, down more than 12.5 percent since December, but posted its highest level against the mark since June 1993.
It was trading at 3.3615 per mark late on Tuesday, drawing ever closer to its central parity rate in the European exchange rate mechanism at 3.3538.

Analysts said, however, they thought it unlikely the Bank of France would allow the franc to climb too quickly to the parity rate. The franc has been gradually appreciating ever since it broke through 3.37, a level many suspected the central bank was defending, on March 27.
